description: USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE FACTORY OF object-class-name-1 (ISO §2023:13.18.60.2; GR22 d)1.a./d)2.a.) — the item holds a class's FACTORY object, not an instance. LIVE since kb/Work PB389 (it was loud-staged COBOL0899 before): the emitted type is the D11 factory singleton class, INVOKE through it resolves the FACTORY method interface (§2023:9.3.6), SET … TO class-name is §2023:14.9.39.3 SR13, and SR12 a)3. makes the FACTORY axis invariant on assignment. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the 1985 USAGE clause's general format (§1985:VI.5.14.2) is `[ USAGE IS ] { BINARY | COMPUTATIONAL | COMP | DISPLAY | INDEX | PACKED-DECIMAL }` and nothing else, its §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR3 naming the numeric usages it has: 'a USAGE clause specifying BINARY, COMPUTATIONAL, or PACKED-DECIMAL must be declared with a PICTURE character-string that describes a numeric item', with no OBJECT REFERENCE alternative; §2002:13.16.58.1 prints `OBJECT REFERENCE [ interface-name-1 | [ FACTORY OF ] ACTIVE-CLASS | [ FACTORY OF ] class-name-1 [ ONLY ] ]`, §2002:F.1 item 6 lists ACTIVE-CLASS, FACTORY and OBJECT-REFERENCE among 'The following reserved words have been added', and §2002:F.2 item 82 states the change: 'Object orientation. Support for object oriented programming has been added.' §2002:13.16.58.3 GR14d.1.a has the phrase's meaning: 'If the FACTORY phrase is specified, the object referenced by this data item shall be the factory object of the specified class or of a subclass of the specified class.' §2014:13.18.60.1 prints the same format and §2014:13.18.60.3 GR21d.1.a the same rule, so 2014 = 2023.

PROGRAM-ID. UORFO.

CLASS-ID. UORFOC.

OBJECT.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.

END CLASS UORFOC.
